def: Removing or switching off one component of a system to measure how much it contributes.
One thing that can be varied in an experiment, such as the learning rate.
A value that a factor takes; two-level designs use off and on.
The average change in a score when one factor goes from low to high, averaged over the other factors' levels.
A case where one factor's effect depends on the level of another.
Changing two things together so that their effects cannot be separated afterwards.
An experiment that runs every combination of the factor levels.
A table with one row per run holding its configuration, seed, code version, environment and results.
A short digest of a configuration in canonical form, so that equal configurations share a key.
Rerunning a stored run from its row and checking that the result matches the original.
